title: Give Dev Team 2's worktree a documented way back, so a close cannot strand on a branch nobody reads

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 52b1846 on main; working tree clean apart from .vscode/settings.json. Sprint file read fresh.

Every requirement met, and the two claims this design actually rests on are true — I checked both against git rather than taking them from the docstring.

================================================================
THE ORDERING GUARANTEE, CHECKED IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS
================================================================

The whole primary-vs-linked detection rests on one thing: `git worktree list` puts the primary first. That is easy to confirm from the primary checkout and prove nothing, because the interesting call happens from INSIDE a linked worktree, where "first" could plausibly mean "the one you're standing in." Checked both, against this repo's own real worktree:

  from the primary  -> worktree /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely
  from the linked   -> worktree /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely

Same answer from both. The primary is listed first regardless of where the command runs, which is the only ordering property the code relies on and the one that would have made it silently wrong.

REQ 1 AND REQ 4 — REPRODUCED END TO END, both directions, in a scratch repo with a real worktree and a real full-gate lifecycle:

  closed from inside the linked worktree:
    Sprint 1 closed. Confirmed: QA1 audit, LiveQA live test, user authorization.
    THIS CLOSE HAS NOT REACHED main. You are on branch 'devteam2/sprint-1', in a linked
    worktree (...), not the primary checkout (...). ... You must NOT push or merge it
    yourself -- only Pipeman ever pushes ... hand off to PIPEMAN by name: branch
    'devteam2/sprint-1', and the commit you just made ...

  closed from the primary checkout:
    Sprint 2 closed. Confirmed: QA1 audit, LiveQA live test, user authorization.
    (silent — no strand statement, correctly)

  main's own view of sprint 1 afterwards:   Phase: dev_build     (still stranded, as expected)

It prints immediately after the success line, in the close's own output, which is the criterion. And the criterion's real test — "a reader who sees only that output knows the record has not landed" — is met by the first six words rather than by something buried mid-paragraph. Leading with "THIS CLOSE HAS NOT REACHED main" instead of a "WARNING:" prefix was the right call; it is the one line in that output that contradicts the line above it, and it needs to win.

REQ 2 — no path added here writes to git. The two subprocess calls are `git worktree list --porcelain` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, both reads. Grepped every added line in the commit for push/merge/rebase/commit/add/reset/checkout: the only hits are inside smoke_test.sh's own sandbox fixtures, nothing in the shipped script. Pipeman is named in capitals in the emitted text and by name in CLAUDE.md step 3, with the branch and the commit-to-report both named. Not a generic "hand off."

REQ 3 — the section now runs create -> work -> close -> commit -> hand off -> remove, as four numbered steps after the existing create/work prose. A Dev Team 2 session reading only that section knows what to do at the end, which is exactly what was missing. Step 1 also explains why this is a statement and not a gate — a refusal would leave Dev Team 2 with no legal action, since it cannot push past it — which is the transition-precondition rule applied correctly rather than cited.

REQ 5 — both factual claims about `git worktree remove` verified directly against a real worktree, because guidance that is confidently wrong about a destructive command is worse than no guidance:

  uncommitted/untracked files present  -> "fatal: ... contains modified or untracked files,
                                           use --force to delete it", directory still there
  clean directory, UNMERGED branch     -> removed without complaint

So the distinction the section draws is real: refusing-on-dirty is not the same guarantee as merged. And the check it recommends works — `git branch --merged main | grep devteam2/sprint-9` returned nothing before the merge and the branch name after. The "never remove a directory a session might still be cd'd into" instruction is there, with the reason attached.

TESTS — falsified in both directions, against a clean full copy with a green baseline first:

  strand warning never printed        -> FAILS: "closing from inside a worktree must print the
                                                 unmissable strand statement (Req 1/4)"
  warning printed from the primary too -> FAILS: "closing from the primary checkout must never
                                                  print the strand statement (false positive)"

The negative case is the one I most expected to be decorative and it isn't. A check like this earns its keep by staying silent in the ordinary case, and that property is now protected rather than assumed.

SUITE: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED, TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.2.7".

VERSION — npm ends at 0.2.6 with `latest` pointing there, so 0.2.7 is correct and necessary.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL — none of these is worth a round
- Detached HEAD in a linked worktree: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the literal "HEAD", so the statement reads "You are on branch 'HEAD'" and would tell Pipeman to merge a branch by that name. The warning still fires, which is the part that matters, and /sprint-worktree always creates `-b devteam2/sprint-<N>`, so this framework never produces a detached worktree itself. Worth a `if branch_name == "HEAD"` nudge whenever that function is next open.
- CLAUDE.md's "an unmerged branch with a clean directory removes without complaint and takes its commits nowhere" — accurate in intent, slightly loose in wording: removing the worktree does not delete the branch, so the commits remain reachable through it. "Takes its commits nowhere" could be misread as "loses them." The operative instruction (check merged first) is correct either way.
- If git is missing or unreadable, the check returns None and a worktree close strands silently. Consistent with every other divergence check in this file and documented as such; noting it so it is not rediscovered as a bug.
- The version-bump omission is now five sprints running (30, 31, 32, 33, 34). This is a sprint-template fix for Master Controller to make once. I will stop re-flagging it after this.
- Long-carried: every launcher allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 34, Pipeman ships 52b1846 and publishes 0.2.7.

For LiveQA: Req 1's criterion is explicit that confirming the text exists is NOT enough — the test is whether a reader seeing only that output knows the record has not landed. Read it cold, as if you had not seen this sprint, and say whether you would have understood you were stranded. Req 4 is the narrower mechanical half of the same check. And the whole-sprint criterion is the real one: run the sequence that produced this sprint and confirm it either cannot strand or cannot strand silently.
commit=f91a3e8 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for f91a3e8e3af678e443075f1dda083031285e0707 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.2.7 by re-running the exact sequence that stranded sprint 32. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, 2026-09-10. No billed agent runs.

PROVENANCE
0.2.7 on the registry; dist-tags.latest 0.2.7; gitHead f91a3e8e3af678e443075f1dda083031285e0707 == last_shipped_commit; zero `reshipped` events. Content check per sprint 13's rule: all 63 published files byte-identical to `git show f91a3e8:<path>`, MISMATCHED 0, tarball sha1 matches the registry's dist.shasum.

I should declare an interest before the rest of this: I was a participant in the failure this sprint fixes. Sprint 32's verdict was mine, and the stall that followed involved my record sitting somewhere Dev Team could not read. That gives me unusually direct standing on Req 1's cold read and also a reason to be careful, since I already know the answer the message is trying to convey.

================================================================
WHOLE-SPRINT CRITERION — THE SEQUENCE RE-RUN: PASS. IT CANNOT STRAND SILENTLY.
================================================================
Ran the original shape end to end on a real install: created the sprint in the primary checkout, made a worktree with the shipped `dev2_worktree.sh`, then took the sprint from `start` through both gates to `complete_ready` and closed it — all inside the worktree.

The close succeeded, and then said so about itself:

  "THIS CLOSE HAS NOT REACHED main. You are on branch 'devteam2/sprint-1', in a linked worktree
   (/private/tmp/s34-devteam2-sprint-1), not the primary checkout (/private/tmp/s34). Committing the
   bookkeeping this just wrote records it HERE, on this branch, and nowhere else -- main, origin, and
   every other checkout will keep reading this sprint as still open until someone merges this branch
   in. You must NOT push or merge it yourself -- only Pipeman ever pushes, no exception, and that
   holds here too. Commit this bookkeeping now (CLAUDE.md's own commit rule), then hand off to PIPEMAN
   by name: branch 'devteam2/sprint-1', and the commit you just made (`git rev-parse HEAD` after
   committing). See CLAUDE.md's "Running two sprints at once" section for the full close -> return ->
   remove sequence, including when the worktree directory itself is safe to remove."

THE WARNING IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATIVE — checked rather than assumed. Req 1 allows either outcome: main reads `complete`, or the close says loudly that it doesn't. It is the second, and I confirmed the premise:
  main registry status: todo
  main phase:           no state file at all
  main's copy of the file: docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-1_stranded-close-redux.md
So the close genuinely did not reach main, and the message is the only thing standing between that fact and a silent stall. Had main read `complete`, the warning would have been noise; it doesn't, so it isn't.

AND IT STAYS QUIET WHEN IT SHOULD. Control: the identical sprint driven to close in the primary checkout, no worktree. Occurrences of "HAS NOT REACHED main": 0. Just the write receipt and the close confirmation. This is the property sprints 25 and 29 established for their own signals, and it holds here — a warning that fired on every close would be filtered out within a week, and this one fires only on the shape that actually strands.

================================================================
REQ 1 — THE COLD READ, ANSWERED DIRECTLY
================================================================
QA1's framing: confirming the text exists is explicitly not enough; would *I*, seeing only that output, have understood the record had not landed?

Yes — and I can be more specific than a yes, because I can name what each part does for a reader who knows nothing:
  - It leads with the failure, in capitals, immediately after the success line. The close reports two
    things and the second contradicts the comfortable reading of the first. That ordering is the work.
  - It tells me where I am in terms I can verify: branch name, this worktree's path, and the primary
    checkout's path, so I do not have to know what "linked worktree" means to check which one I'm in.
  - It pre-empts the wrong fix specifically: committing "records it HERE, on this branch, and nowhere
    else." A reader who has just been told to commit their bookkeeping by the line above would
    otherwise reasonably conclude that committing finishes the job.
  - It names who consumes the handoff, by role, in capitals — PIPEMAN — rather than "hand off".
  - It gives the two facts Pipeman actually needs (branch name, and the commit, with the command to
    obtain it) rather than leaving me to work out what to include.
  - It forecloses the tempting shortcut: "You must NOT push or merge it yourself."

BUT THE HONEST VERSION OF THE COUNTERFACTUAL, since I lived the original: in sprint 32 nobody misread a message. There was no message. The close succeeded, said nothing about reach, and the divergence surfaced later and elsewhere — as a cross-tree warning at status time telling Dev Team a verdict *might* exist in another tree. They correctly refused to act on "might", and that refusal is what cost the round.

So the fix is not "clearer wording than before". It is a statement where there was silence, at the moment of the action rather than at someone else's later read. That is a genuinely different class of change, and it is the right one: the person who can still fix the problem cheaply is the one who just ran the close, not the one who discovers it two sessions later.

================================================================
REQ 4 — THE STATEMENT IS IN THE CLOSE'S OWN OUTPUT: PASS
================================================================
The mechanical half. It appears in the output of `complete` itself, in the same stream, in the same invocation — not in a subsequent `status` call, not in a log a reader would have to think to check. A Dev Team 2 session that runs the close and reads nothing else still sees it.

================================================================
CARRIED, NOT TESTED, AND SAYING SO
================================================================
QA1's three informational nits, recorded because they should survive this gate rather than live only in a relay message. I did not test any of them — they are outside my criteria and QA1 characterised each as non-blocking:
 - A detached HEAD in a linked worktree reads as branch 'HEAD' in the warning. Cosmetic here because
   this framework's own `/sprint-worktree` never produces a detached worktree.
 - CLAUDE.md's "takes its commits nowhere" phrasing is loose: removing a worktree does not delete the
   branch, and the commits stay reachable through it.
 - A missing git binary makes the check silently no-op, by design, consistent with every other
   divergence check in the file.
And the fourth: the package.json version-bump omission from Requirements is now five sprints running (30-34), which is a sprint-template fix for Master Controller. QA1 says they are done re-raising it, which seems right — a defect re-flagged five times without being fixed has stopped being information.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result here I produced directly against published 0.2.7, driving the real commands through a real worktree created by the shipped script. Main's staleness after the close I verified from main's own registry, phase and file location rather than inferring it from the warning's claim about itself — the warning asserts the close did not reach main, and I checked that independently before crediting it.

No corrections to my own method this round.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. The sequence that stranded sprint 32 now announces itself at the moment it happens, to the person still holding the pieces, with the branch and commit they need to hand over and an explicit instruction not to push it themselves. Main is still stale afterwards — that is unchanged and correct, since fixing it would require a push this role must not make — but it can no longer be stale *silently*, which is the whole difference between a two-session stall and a handoff.

Nothing carries forward from this sprint beyond QA1's four informational items above. Two older items remain open and unchanged: the hollow-green CI case is still unobserved, and the permission anchor is now six CLI versions behind this machine.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 34.
